_doc: Registration of the National Archives / Historic Urban Plans reproduction of Wright 1834 against the BPL master this project already traces. Pixel coordinates under `nara_px` are in THIS sheet's own space (5050 x 6628). Generated by tools/register_wright_nara.py — the fit and the correspondences are computed; the control checks, the scale bar and the lacunae are read by eye and hand-written.

method.note: Patches are placed on a blind grid over the BPL sheet and located in the NARA sheet by normalised cross-correlation. A patch below ncc_floor is carried in the record and excluded from the fit.

fit_nara_to_bpl.type: affine, least squares, NARA/HUP pixel -> BPL pixel

fit_nara_to_utm.type: affine, NARA/HUP pixel -> EPSG:26916, composed with the BPL fit

control_checks.feature: State St & Madison St, centre of the crossing
control_checks.method: Read by eye off gridded crops of BOTH sheets at 1.5-2.3x, to the same rule (centre of the street crossing, or the named block corner). Picking precision about +/- 8 px on each sheet, so a residual under ~16 px is two picks agreeing.

control_checks.method: Read by eye off gridded crops of BOTH sheets at 1.5-2.3x, to the same rule (centre of the street crossing, or the named block corner). Picking precision about +/- 8 px on each sheet, so a residual under ~16 px is two picks agreeing.

control_check_note: The eight GCPs in wright_1834_gcps.json are NOT re-picked here. They carry their own picking error against modern control (1.8 to 32.7 m), and re-picking them on a second sheet would mix that error into a measurement of how the two sheets differ. So four of the eight neighbourhoods were instead read ON BOTH SHEETS by one hand to one rule, and the residual below is what is left after the fitted affine carries the new sheet's reading onto the old one. It runs 11.7 to 20.4 px (8.3 to 14.5 m), it changes sign across the sheet — G1 is +17 px in x and G7 is -15 px — and that is the two DRAWINGS disagreeing locally, which is what two hand-drawn renderings of one survey do. It is the same order as the 17.5 m RMS the BPL fit already carries against modern control: a feature read on this sheet and brought through this affine is no worse founded than one read on the BPL sheet, and no better.

scale_bar._doc: Wright draws 'Scale of feet' at the foot of both sheets, ticked 1200 / 600 / 300 and then 200 / 100 / 50 in a finer division at the right. Tick positions below are CENTROIDS of the dark columns in the bar band, not eye picks: the column-darkness profile of the band is thresholded and each run's centroid taken. Only the three long ticks are fitted — the short right-hand divisions are hand-drawn and sit 9 percent off a linear reading of their own labels, which is a statement about the draughtsman's hand and not about the sheet's scale.
scale_bar.against_the_fits: The bar is drawn horizontally and therefore measures the x direction, which is the axis to compare it on. This sheet: bar 0.6889 m/px against 0.6975 from the chained affine, 1.2 percent apart. The BPL sheet: bar 0.7018 against 0.6983 from its own GCP fit, 0.5 percent apart. Over the bar's own length — 1200 ft, 366 m — 1.2 percent is 4.5 m, comfortably inside the 17.5 m RMS that fit carries, so neither bar is a finding against its sheet. The two BARS do disagree with each other by 1.87 percent while the line work registers at 0.16 percent; with about 1 percent of reading uncertainty in each bar fit that is a weak signal, and the honest reading is that the bars were ruled by hand on each sheet separately. Measure distance through the affine, never off either bar.

lacunae._doc: The sheet's caption: 'Signs of wear are apparent. Two portions are missing, the larger being near the lower center. At one time the drawing was torn to this spot from the upper right margin. Later the manuscript was mounted on cloth to repair this tear and to prevent further damage.' Boxes are in this sheet's pixel space so that a later reading knows what it cannot have read. ONE loss was found, not two; the second is recorded as not located rather than guessed at.

regions.where: The South Branch, against the west side of School Section blocks 87 and 88 — the 'Reserved' pair. The caption's larger missing portion, and it is 'near the lower center' as the caption says.
regions.what_is_gone: The river's west bank line through about 150 px of its course, the north-west corner of the Reserved block outline, and the first letters of the word 'Reserved' written across block 88. The blocks' numerals 87 and 88 themselves survive.
regions.found_by: White backing showing through: mean luminance above 235 with saturation below 0.12 against a tan sheet, one connected region of ~9,400 px, confirmed by eye at 3x.

regions.where: Running up and to the right from L1 across School Section blocks 112, 113, 114 and 115.
regions.note: A crease, not a loss: the paper is continuous and every numeral crossing it is legible. This is the segment of the caption's tear that can be seen; it points at the upper right margin, as the caption says, but was traced only over the stretch where it is unambiguous.

regions.where: A dark green-brown band across the top of the drawing, from the west edge to the North Division block work.
regions.note: Discoloured and ragged, with no ink lost — consistent with a mounted repair or a fold, and it is the only other sheet-wide damage in the drawn area. Graded inferred because nothing on the sheet says which it is.

regions.where: The sheet's top edge in the upper right quadrant.
regions.note: Chipped and ragged along its whole length, in the margin the caption names as where the tear entered. No drawn work falls inside it.

lacunae.second_portion: NOT LOCATED. The caption says two portions are missing and only one loss is visible in the drawn area: a search for white backing over the whole sheet returns L1 and nothing else above 1,000 px, and the three next-largest candidates are the unpainted centres of 'Reserved' blocks and the blank left margin. The second portion may lie in the margin, may be small enough to read as chipping along the top edge (D2), or may have been made good before this reproduction was photographed. Recorded as unfound rather than assigned to any of those.
